newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO COACH PULLS CORK ON TENSION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO COACH PULLS CORK ON TENSION.

text.p: "The only pressure we're feeling is in the beer we're going to drink afterwards," Monaco coach Jean Tigana said on Friday as he tried to defuse tension ahead of Sunday's clash with Paris St Germain.
The French first division leader's match at the Louis II stadium could prove decisive for visitors PSG who will fall seven points behind Monaco if they lose.
Tigana, uncharacteristically chatty and jovial after barely a word for reporters earlier in the week, predicted a clean game despite the tension.
"We're all adults in both camps and there have never been problems on the pitch (between the two sides)," he said.
"It will be a very tight, physical match like all matches at the highest level and it will be played in the best spirit."

Tigana, part of a brilliant midfield in the France team that won the European championship in 1984, was more concerned with the poor state of the Louis II pitch where Monaco have struggled in their most recent home games.
He said that despite the importance of the match, there were another 14 in the league "and against Paris there are only three points at stake.
"Next week we go to Lyon and there are also three points in play," Tigana said.
"It's true that (with a win) we would be in a favourable position, but...Paris were eight points in front of us and that didn't perturb us at the time."
Tigana said recent setbacks, for Monaco in the French Cup and PSG in the European Super Cup, would not affect either side.
"After a match, after a disappointment the players quickly forget and concentrate on other objectives," he said.
"Our elimination from the French Cup has had no influence on our work and state of mind and there are no external or internal problems."
